messages:
alex: noticed a burst of NVMe read/retry errors in asia-southeast1 (scratchpool cohort d-22) around 21:03 UTC, GPU attaches timing out. attaching alert and quick logs. anyone on call? :eyes:

infra-bot: ALERT host-group=d-22 metric=nvme_read_retries delta=+89 window=10m threshold=40 flagged=[d-22-01,d-22-04,d-22-09]

toni_ops: oncall, looking. first question: are we seeing kernel CRCs or just retry counters?

alex: both. kernel shows read retry then CRC on a few blocks. nodes still online but attach latency is spiking to ~20s. dmesg snippet below:

--- dmesg ---
[21:02:41] nvme0n1: async read failed, retrying (status 0x2)
[21:02:46] nvme0n1: CRC mismatch, lba=0x12345
[21:02:52] nvme0n1: SMART Critical Warn: media_errors=3
--- end ---

rahul_sre: initial hypothesis: background snapshot compaction + janitor scrub overlapping caused short-lived write/read amplification on some hosts. can we throttle snapshot job and reduce janitor concurrency for the cohort? also move GPU scheduling off these nodes.

jackson: agree. plan: 1) patch snapshot controller to avoid d-22 cohort for 60m 2) cordon affected nodes 3) reduce janitor to 3 threads for cohort d-22 4) bump alert sensitivity for this group.

toni_ops: quick cost tradeoff: moving work to reserved pool will increase per-minute cost, but avoids customer visible attach failures. what's estimated duration?

alex: if throttling snapshot + janitor tweak holds, 1.5-3h to drain the backlog. if SMART trend keeps rising, we'll need 4-drive replacement per rack which is a longer ops flow.

infra-bot: NOTE snapshot-controller: patched excludeSelector=cohort=d-22 for 60m by jackson

jackson: executed: `kubectl cordon d-22-01 d-22-04 && kubectl drain d-22-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`; patched configmap `scratchpool-d22` to `janitor.max_concurrency=3`

rahul_sre: also adding a temporary scheduler policy: prefer nodes with local-ssd-health=good label, fallback to reserved pool. pushed canary for 10 nodes.

toni_ops: i've opened cost watch: reserved routing estimated extra infra spend ~USD 180 for next 3 hours if we route all affected GPU pods. if we need RMAs, capex for 4 drives ~USD 3.2k plus verification.

alex: monitoring SMART attributes 0x0b/0x0c (power cycles/temp) and media_errors. setting a short-lived alert to trigger if media_errors delta > 10 in 30m.

infra-bot: METRIC_UPDATE cohort=d-22 metric=nvme_media_errors delta=+2 window=5m

jackson: scrub on d-22-09 started in isolated mode to avoid cluster-wide load. nvme smart-log run scheduled every 5m via playbook.

alex: scrub shows reduced retries after we paused snapshots. d-22-09 normalized, uncordoning d-22-09 now. keeping d-22-01 and d-22-04 cordoned until stable for 45m.

rahul_sre: follow-up runbook items added: - throttle snapshot compaction windows to off-peak - add label/placement to avoid scheduling heavy background IO near expected GPU attach windows - lower janitor concurrency on cohorts with >2 media_errors

toni_ops: noted. i'll start a spare parts check and pre-authorize RMA if two more hosts hit media_errors within 24h.

alex: summary: software mitigations (pause snapshot, lower janitor, cordon) resolved immediate attach latency; two hosts under watch with SMART counters. if counters spike again we'll schedule RMA batch. will post final after 4h watch. :thumbsup:

jackson: thanks team. closing temporary routing cost monitor, leaving incident watch open.

infra-bot: RESOLVE alert=nvme_read_retries cohort=d-22 reason=mitigation_applied time=21:22:05 UTC

alex: 4h check-in: d-22-01 media_errors stable at +0 over last 2h, d-22-04 still +1. marking this as non-critical for now. end thread.
